title: Choose the visual world for Lanes
question: The roll assigned the Carrom Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Carrom Board
options.lineage: The lacquered carrom board found in nearly every Sri Lankan home
options.thesis: Home is the board: four workspaces sit on four sides, and today's deep task is the red queen in the centre.
materials: double-ruled baselines ending in red rings
options.viewport: A dark frame rail on the left holds the level bar and nav. The birch field centres on a queen medallion holding today's deep task. Each workspace runs as a double-ruled baseline with its open projects as coins, ringed in that workspace's colour.
options.risk: If the rosette and rings take over, it turns into a game board costume. They must stay as the one signature move on a plain, standard dashboard.

raised.raise: Stage state is shown by line form, not colour: solid for live, dashed for waiting, half-height for stale. Colour stays reserved for workspaces.
Codes come first. Every project and task leads with its handle (GK, L-50), set in tabular figures, so the catalogue scans by code.
Workspace colour owns whole regions (each baseline band and its header field), not 8px dots.
On a phone, the queen (today's deep task) owns the first screen on its own. Everything else is one scroll below.

options.label: House Sports Meet
options.lineage: Sri Lankan school sports meets: house colours, track lanes, the points board
options.thesis: Each workspace is a school house running in its own lane, and the week is scored on the house points board.
options.viewport: A top bar sets the four houses as lanes with progress along each. Under it sits a points board table for the week, then today's routine as the event programme.
options.risk: The most literal reading of the name 'Lanes'. It's familiar, and the bunting could tip it into school-poster territory.

options.label: Tabbed Reference Manual
options.lineage: Boxed-software manuals with coloured section dividers
options.thesis: Each workspace is a full-strength divider board, and the tab rail down the edge is the nav, sized by how much each one holds.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail on the right, one tab per workspace. The open workspace's hue fills the board behind translucent panels for the deep task, routine and progress.
options.case: It fuses cleanly. The section hues map exactly to workspace colours and the tab rail is a clear nav, but you have no personal connection to boxed manuals.
options.risk: Full-hue boards are loud on a page you open every morning, which strains the 'quiet by default' rule.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.lineage: Friendly consumer apps with a thumb-reachable bottom bar
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, and the one bright colour on screen is always something you can press.
options.viewport: A single card column with the deep task card first, then routine and progress. A bottom bar on the phone, a slim rail on the laptop.
options.case: Very clear, and the bottom bar fixes mobile navigation, but it says nothing about how your work actually runs.
options.risk: It's close to the category default, so Lanes would look like any habit app.

options.label: Emission-line Rail
options.thesis: Every element registers against one rail, and state is shown by line form.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with each destination as a tick.
options.risk: Cold and lab-like for a personal tracker.
options.case: Loses on both axes: it isn't from your world, and a single rail hides the four workspaces.
options.kept: State shown by line form (solid, dashed, half-height), not by hue.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every item has a catalogue number, and colour codes stand in for words.
options.viewport: A fac-numbered index on matte black.
options.risk: Hiding names behind codes hurts quick scanning.
options.case: Loses on both axes: replacing words with codes hurts clarity.
options.kept: Every project and task leads with its code (GK, L-50).

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Every area is a swelling lobe of flat colour.
options.risk: Organic lobes fight a dense working screen.
options.case: Loses on both axes: playful lobes hide state.
options.kept: Workspace colour owns whole regions, not dots.

options.label: Vertical Media Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the whole viewport at a time.
options.viewport: A single item fills the screen and the next is one flick away.
options.risk: A dashboard needs overview, not one item at a time.
options.case: Loses on both axes: it's the opposite of an overview.
options.kept: On a phone, the deep task owns the first screen on its own.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, modern productivity dashboard like Linear or Things, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A left sidebar, a greeting header, a KPI row, then cards for focus, routine and workspaces.
canonCard.risk: It looks like every other productivity app.
